=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- tests/test_judge_semble_prefetch_contract.py:99-118 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: The test checks for placeholder resolution and footer presence, but does not verify block ordering or full output completeness.
  WHY: A regression that swaps or interleaves the workflow restriction and Semble blocks could still pass this test while producing the wrong judge prompt.
- scripts/targeted_file_context.py:412-472 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_1-fast, deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The SEMBLE_QUERY and SEMBLE_FALLBACK telemetry report only the clamped chunk count and do not indicate that clamping occurred.
  WHY: Operators cannot distinguish a requested high chunk count from a clamped value without cross-referencing the original input; the reviewers disagree on whether this is a bug or an observability hardening issue.
- scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh:351-476 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_1-fast, deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: Identifiers extracted into the Semble query are capped at 40 items, but individual identifier strings are not length-bounded before being joined into the query text.
  WHY: A pathologically long identifier could bloat the query and reduce retrieval quality; the reviewers disagree on whether this is a runtime bug or a hardening concern.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh:395-402 | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: Individual identifier strings extracted from CI capture output are appended to the query text without per-identifier length bounding.
  WHY: A very long identifier could bloat the Semble query text; the reviewer frames this as a hardening concern rather than a correctness defect.
- scripts/targeted_file_context.py:454-454 | severity=low | confidence=1
  PROBLEM: When `_normalize_semble_max_chunks()` clamps the requested chunk count, the telemetry reports only the clamped value and does not indicate that clamping occurred.
  WHY: Operators cannot distinguish a deliberately low chunk count from a clamped-high request without cross-referencing the CLI argument.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
